subtopics.title: Quick-Fire Recall Across Micro and Contemporary Issues

questions.question: Oligopoly firms following the dominant firm's price without any agreement are practising:
A market where ONE large producer can supply everyone more cheaply than several smaller ones could is a:
Prices still rising, but more slowly than before — the term is:
Enjoying a good without paying because nobody can be excluded from it is called:
options: Free riding — the reason public goods need the state

subtopics.title: Short Answers: Quick Marks on Market Concepts

questions.question: Name TWO barriers to entry that protect a monopolist. A full-mark pair is:
Why does a maximum price set BELOW equilibrium create a shortage? The two-mark answer is:
options: Suppliers produce more at lower prices
Quantity demanded rises while quantity supplied falls, so buyers outnumber the goods available

questions.question: When a short item says 'name' or 'list', the right response is:
options: The items only — the mark pays for the item, not the speech around it
A definition of every term in the question

subtopics.title: Data Response: The Monopolist's Graph, Described and Solved

questions.question: On the described graph, equilibrium quantity of 80 units sits where:
options: The demand curve meets the vertical axis

questions.question: The monopolist's marginal revenue lies BELOW its demand curve because:
options: Selling one more unit means lowering the price on ALL units, so the last unit adds less than its price

questions.question: Price R200, average cost R160, quantity 80. Total economic profit is:
options: R3 200 — forty rand per unit times eighty units

questions.question: If average cost had been R200 and price R160 at the same quantity, the identical method chain would show:
options: An economic loss of R3 200 — the procedure never changes, only the direction of the gap

subtopics.title: Data Response: Inflation Figures and the Weighted Basket

questions.question: The consumer price index is published by:
The index moves from 130,0 to 139,1. The inflation rate is:
options: 7,0 percent — the change of 9,1 divided by the OLD index of 130,0, times 100
6,5 percent — dividing by the new index

questions.question: Food weighted 50% up 8%, transport 30% up 5%, education 20% up 3%. The weighted increase is:
If fuel and electricity lead the increases, the inflation is best described as:
options: Demand-pull, cured by higher interest rates alone
Cost-push — and a higher repo rate cools spending but cannot cheapen fuel

subtopics.title: Paragraph Answers: Graphs in Words and Judgements in Context

questions.question: A ten-mark paragraph answer in this practice set is built from:
options: Five developed facts at two marks each, with a verbal graph able to stand in for one
One drawn diagram with no words
A copied definition repeated five times

questions.question: A perfect competitor earns only NORMAL profit in the long run because:
options: Free entry brings newcomers chasing profit, supply rises and price falls to the lowest point of average cost

questions.question: A strong case AGAINST the sugary drinks levy is that:
options: It raises no revenue at all
It is regressive, can cost jobs in the sugar value chain, and consumers may switch to untaxed sweet foods

questions.question: In a proposal paragraph on township tourism, the second mark of every pair is earned by:
options: The justification — explaining the mechanism through which the proposal works

subtopics.title: The Essay, Built Live: Compare and Contrast Market Structures

questions.question: The mark plan of this session's thirty-mark practice essay is:
options: Definition 2, main body 20, evaluation 6, closing judgement 2

questions.question: The individual perfect competitor's demand curve, against the monopolist's, is:
options: Horizontal at the market price against downward-sloping with marginal revenue below it

questions.question: In the monopoly's long-run equilibrium, economic profit can persist because:
options: Barriers hold entry out, so price can remain above average cost

questions.question: A balanced six-mark evaluation of monopoly would argue that:
options: Scale economies can justify regulated natural monopolies, but unregulated monopoly transfers welfare from consumers — so policy watches structure

subtopics.title: A Second Essay Plan: Combating Inflation, Built to Its Marks

questions.question: The DIRECT policy answer to demand-pull inflation is:
options: Raising the repo rate to cool consumption and investment

questions.question: Discipline over administered prices such as electricity tariffs fights inflation by:
options: Attacking a cost-push engine directly, since these prices feed into every producer's costs

questions.question: An honest evaluation of inflation targeting in South Africa concludes that it has:
options: Delivered credibility more reliably than comfort, and needs fiscal policy rowing the same way
Replaced the need for any other policy

questions.question: The session-wide checklist for calculations says full marks require:
options: The setup line, the workings and the answer labelled with sign and units
